result:
Round 88 is planned. The decision is **CONTINUE**: round 87 failed on one medium layout bug, even though every one of its 18 checks passed.

**What C found in round 87** (checked independently in a real browser at both screen sizes)
- Moving WAV encoding off the main thread worked. On a 5-minute project the UI's worst stall fell from 445 ms to 105–107 ms for WAV and 97–111 ms for MP3. Progress shows for each phase, and a second MP3 export now works in the same page after a timeout.
- **The bug (R87-PROGRESS-BELOW-FOLD-1280):** at 1280×720 the progress label is cut off, and the progress bar and the busy button sit below the visible part of the Export dialog. The dialog was already 12 px too tall before any export.
- Gate 87 was skipped because C failed the round, so nothing is published. HEAD is still `971141d`, and the round-87 work stays uncommitted in the tree as the new baseline.

**Round 88 task** (one bug, one owner, three files)
- **Fix:** in `ArrangementExportDialog.tsx`, the status message, progress, overload warning and buttons go into one footer that stays pinned to the bottom of the dialog. The order of elements and the Tab order don't change, and the shared `Modal.tsx` is not touched.
- **Focus guard:** a small handler scrolls the dialog when a focused control would be hidden behind the footer. The advisor's second review caught a flaw in my first draft. The existing code focuses the dialog's outer wrapper when an export starts, so the guard would have scrolled the dialog on its own at every export click. The guard now skips that wrapper, with a test, a mutation check and a C row for it.
- **Tests:** a new test file (FT1–FT4) checks structure and the scroll arithmetic only, because the unit-test environment has no real layout. Whether things are actually visible is C's browser check.
- **C checks visibility, not just presence:** each element must be inside the dialog's visible area and be what the browser finds at its centre point. That gap is how round 87 passed on DOM evidence alone. There is also a focus check and a short re-run of the progress, keyboard and responsiveness checks.
- A changes exactly three files, so the project rule makes A's code-reviewer run required.

**Records updated from C's evidence only**
- Nothing is marked done. The 18 stage-3a results are recorded, the medium bug is open, and the same-page MP3 retry fix is verified but not yet published.
- I did not fold in C's other note: the timeout message still says "reload the page", which is no longer true. Fixing it would pull more files into a fix round, so it is a new Low in the Lows batch.
- The reviewer's architecture note is recorded as a signal for the planned architecture checkpoint after stage 3b, not as a task.
- I've asked root again to test the production build at gate 88, since gate 87 never ran.

**Next:** if C passes round 88, root can publish rounds 87 and 88 together. Round 89 is the regression round if it's planned on or after 2026-10-24; otherwise it is stage 3b (Cancel, abort on unmount, the WAV + MP3 delivery note).

The advisor was available and I consulted it twice, before writing and before finishing. I did not change any app source: git status is unchanged (17 entries) and all 505 frozen files verify.
